messages:
Sam Carter: FYI — Acme Health procurement insists on Azure Marketplace invoicing. They still want a 12-month reserved commit for 100M tokens/mo. Can marketplace + reserved commit work with our standard commit discounts?
Anya Li: short answer: yes, but take rate matters. Azure take ~12% (depends on offer type) so the effective discount to the customer changes unless we do a private offer.
Jordan Park: also flag: customer wants VPC/private deployment (on-prem-like). Marketplace usually covers hosted API SKU only — Dedicated/Private needs a separate contract. Procurement says "must be on marketplace for AP/PO reasons."
Sam Carter: ok. tradeoffs: 1) marketplace public offer = fast but take-rate reduces our net, so discount to customer has to be adjusted; 2) marketplace private offer = can present negotiated pricing and honor commit appearance to procurement, but ops/legal + marketplace lead time.
Lee Morales: finance note: marketplace invoicing flows through MSFT; revenue recognition and refund/credits handling differ. If we push a direct contract we can apply deeper commit discounts w/out marketplace cuts. For private offers we need to create an Azure Private Offer (APO) and include our negotiated unit prices + term. APO still goes through marketplace but keeps negotiated pricing intact.
Anya Li: examples: if list price token cost = $0.0006, direct commit 20% off => $0.00048. If Azure takes 12% and we keep same list, effective customer price will be higher unless we compensate. We usually do either: a) increase our list discount in the private offer to net the customer target, or b) absorb part of take rate (needs deal desk ok).
Jordan Park: technical constraint for POC: they need dedicated capacity for data isolation and long-running KV cache. Marketplace flows can't provision Dedicated in our Dedicated pool automatically. We need SOW + provisioning ticket. Procurement still wants a single invoice via marketplace.
Sam Carter: timeline: procurement needs paperwork by Friday EOD to hit their quarter. Can we get a private offer created + deal-desk approval this week?
FinanceOps Bot: @Sam Carter I can start the APO prep. Need these items: 1) committed SKU list and quantities 2) target net price per token 3) legal term length 4) customer billing entity + Azure tenant ID 5) PO template. APO creation lead time: 3–5 business days once submitted.
Lee Morales: Deal desk note: if we want to absorb >5% of marketplace take rate we need CFO approval. For anything that changes revenue recognition (credits, extended grace, custom refund terms) legal review required.
Anya Li: action items from my side: draft private offer pricing that nets the customer same effective price as our direct commit. I'll add a cost column showing our margin vs. net after marketplace take.
Jordan Park: I'll create the provisioning runbook for Dedicated + POC steps and an engineer to standby for the week of deployment. POC duration requested: 2 weeks, starting after APO acceptance.
Sam Carter: ok — I'll assemble the deal packet and submit to deal-desk. Packet will contain: proposed APO pricing, commit SOW, PO template, Azure tenant ID (from buyer), POC runbook, and negotiation point list (we may ask to split take-rate).
Lee Morales: pinging @Anya Li and @FinanceOps Bot for accounting code mapping. We need SKU mapping to internal GL codes so invoice reconciliation doesn't stall procurement.
FinanceOps Bot: confirm — send SKU list to finance@redwood.com and cc billing@redwood.com. I'll create the APO ticket after we have tenant ID + final prices.
Sam Carter: procurement asked if we can do a "marketplace invoice but payable to their parent entity" — that's a legal invoicing nuance. Legal needs to confirm third-party billing name changes. I'll loop in legal. :eyes:
Anya Li: provisional numbers and a short comparison table will be in the packet by 4pm today. Will include two options: (A) Direct contract with deepest net discount (preferred economics for us), (B) Azure Private Offer that matches customer net price but requires APO lead time and CFO sign-off if we absorb >5% take.
Jordan Park: tagged engineer: lee-eng will standby for provisioning once APO accepted.
Sam Carter: perfect. If deal-desk can greenlight absorbing 3% to match price, we get this done this week. Otherwise we present the options and procurement decides. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
